query: The vertices of 30 regions whose resting hyperaligned fine-grained connectivity was most predictive of general intelligence (25.3–31.2% VAF) had a distribution that was similar to that for hyperaligned task connectivity, sharing 68.3% of cortical vertices (compare Figure 3D, Figure 4D), with vertices mostly in the default mode network (49.0%) and smaller parts in the frontoparietal (19.4%), dorsal attention (15.8%), and ventral attention (10.0%) systems (Figure 4E; see also Appendix 1—figure 11).
